recentEvents.title: Ukraine: Returns to unsafe frontline areas: drivers of return and intentions to stay in Khersonska, Zaporizka and Sumska Oblasts, November 2026 [EN/UK]
recentEvents.ai_summary: The update highlights ongoing returns to unsafe frontline areas in Ukraine, particularly in Khersonska, Zaporizka, and Sumska Oblasts, indicating a persistent humanitarian concern amidst active conflict. The situation remains critical as military actions continue to threaten civilian safety and infrastructure, necessitating heightened awareness and caution for those in or considering travel to these regions.
recentEvents.diff_before: Source: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Ukraine Conflict Monitor Update Russia is targeting Ukrainian healthcare facilities and workers ahead of winter while Ukraine targets Russian oil infrastructure. 1,789 conflict events
recentEvents.diff_after: Source: REACH Initiative Introduction Between June and July 2026, REACH in partnership with local NGOs Unity and Strength and Tenth of April conducted three assessments on unsafe returns (returns within 30 kilometres of the front line and/or the border with the Russian Federation) in Khersonska, Sumska and Zaporizka Oblasts. Interviewing 89 returnees with diverse displacement experiences (e.g., displaced abroad, displaced within the oblast), vulnerabilities (e.g., spent savings) and factors of resilience (e.g., owned housing), REACH examined what drove returnees away from “safer” locations, what pulled them to areas with ongoing insecurity, and their needs post-return. Returns to unsafe areas remain a persistent concern for the humanitarian response in Ukraine. An estimated 4.2 million people had returned to their areas of origin or habitual residence as of May 2026.
